# Scenarios

Find your situation, follow its flow. Not sure? Run `/next` (one next step) or `/ask-engr` (which skill fits).

Every flow ends the same way: work lives on a ticket, the ticket ends with evidence, docs stay true. Flows use skills as slash commands; a flow that mentions a skill your install does not have (smaller tiers) can skip that step.

## Starting

| Scenario | Flow |
|---|---|
| New project, idea is clear | `/grill-with-docs` → `/design` (only if data, APIs or boundaries are involved) → `/to-spec` → `/to-tickets` → `/implement` per ticket → `/cut-release` |
| New project, huge or foggy | `/wayfinder` (map of decision tickets, resolved one at a time) → then the line above |
| Existing repo, first time | `/adopt-project` (reads code and docs, creates maps, glossary, first tickets) → continue with the scenario that fits |
| Team handed you documents (TDD, specs, notes, a folder of them) | `/ingest` → `/grill-with-docs` on the gaps → `/to-spec` → `/to-tickets` |
| A decision needs someone else | `/to-questionnaire` → ticket stays `needs-info` until answered |

## Building

| Scenario | Flow |
|---|---|
| Big feature (many slices) | `/grill-with-docs` → `/design` if needed → `/to-spec` → `/to-tickets` → `/implement` per ticket |
| Medium feature (a few slices) | `/grill-with-docs` → `/to-tickets` → `/implement` per ticket |
| Small change (one ticket) | Ask for it. The agent says a ticket is needed first, drafts it, you confirm, then it implements |
| Asked to implement with no ticket | Never start coding. Draft the ticket from the request, get a go-ahead, write it as `in-progress`, then implement (`tickets` skill, "Request with no ticket") |
| Requirements change mid-ticket | Edit that ticket's criteria first, log a "Requirement change" entry, then change code and tests. Different job? New ticket. Contradicts an ADR (Architecture Decision Record)? Supersede it with `/domain-modeling` |
| Whole spec, many tickets | `/implement-spec` (integration branch, parallel subagents) or `loop` for unattended runs |
| Unsure the design works | `/prototype` to answer one question, throw the prototype away, record the answer in the ticket or an ADR |
| Hard-to-reverse choice appears while building | Stop, ask, record an ADR with `/domain-modeling`, link it in the ticket's Inputs |
| Code is tangled or tests are hard to write | `/improve-codebase-architecture` → tickets for the deepening work |
| Team must approve design before code | Design ticket → `/design` → review → dev tickets unblocked (workflow `design-first`) |

## Fixing

| Scenario | Flow |
|---|---|
| Bug reported | `/report-bug` (severity, steps, expected vs actual) → `/triage` → `/implement` with a failing test first (`/tdd`) |
| Cause not obvious, flaky or slow | `/diagnosing-bugs` → `/report-bug` for what it finds → fix as above |
| Bug found while building another ticket | `/report-bug` with "Found during"; do not fix it inside the current ticket unless it blocks it |
| Production incident needing a formal write-up | Workflow `investigation-to-rca`: `/diagnosing-bugs` → `/generate-rca` |
| Intermittent test failures | `/fix-flaky-tests` |

## Reviewing and quality

| Scenario | Flow |
|---|---|
| Review a branch or pull request | `/code-review` (Standards and Spec axes, fresh subagents), findings become tickets or fixes |
| Plan testing for a feature | `/test-strategy` once, then `/test-plan` per spec before `/to-tickets` |
| Automate tests | `/automate-tests` (traced to acceptance criteria) |
| Test by hand, UAT (User Acceptance Testing), regression | `/manual-testing`, bugs via `/report-bug` |
| Go or no-go before release | `/test-report`, then `gate release` |
| Want a second opinion on a plan or idea | `/coach` |

## Teammates and collaboration

| Scenario | Flow |
|---|---|
| Teammates pushed, you pulled | `drift` → `/update-docs` → `drift --mark`; a `doc-drift` ticket records it (workflow `team-sync`) |
| Teammate changed code with no ticket | `drift` still finds it; `/update-docs` fixes facts and drafts `proposed` ADRs for the author to confirm |
| Teammate's change conflicts with your in-progress ticket | Treat it as a requirement change: edit the ticket, log it, adjust code |
| Handing work to another agent, tool or person | `/handoff` (portable summary file) |
| Pasting a lot of reading into a session | `/research` in the background; it saves cited findings to `docs/research/` |

## Shipping and improving

| Scenario | Flow |
|---|---|
| Ready to release | `/cut-release` (gates, version, changelog, notes) |
| Need CI/CD (Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery) | `/setup-pipeline` |
| Pull request description | `/pr` |
| Something went wrong with how the agent worked | `/retro` → improvements to checks, skills or context |

## Learning and asking

| Scenario | Flow |
|---|---|
| How does this code work? | `/ask-repo-question` (read-only) |
| Explain something to me | `/mentor` |
| What can this toolbox do? | `/ask-engr`, `/cli discover` |
| Where are we? | `/next`, `/cli status` |

## When the rules are bent

- **Trivial housekeeping** (typo, formatting, dependency bump): commit with `[no-ticket]`.
- **Guard blocks an edit**: no ticket is `in-progress`. Create one (above), or set `ENGR_GUARD=warn` for the session.
- **Ticket will not close**: `gate deliver --ticket <id>` lists what is missing (criteria not ticked, no test named after a criterion, empty evidence).
- **Lost the thread**: `/next`.
